title: Arc 1b/5: the generated type schema must ACCEPT alias spellings
summary: LCLI-553 shipped alias RESOLUTION but not alias ACCEPTANCE; the regression it exists to fix is still live.
description:
DEFECT IN DELIVERED WORK (LCLI-553, merged in opum-ai/lore-cli#193), found by end-to-end measurement after it landed.

profile.ts:922 pins the type field as z.literal(name), so the Arc type's generated schema accepts ONLY "Arc". An un-migrated document carrying type: Story therefore resolves to the Arc type (the alias works) and is then REJECTED by frontmatter validation:

  error: invalid Story frontmatter in stories/legacy.md: type: Invalid input: expected "Arc"
  hint: fix the field(s) named above to match the type's schema, or run `lore validate`

So `lore link` still refuses an un-migrated document. The failure has MOVED from the coupling gate to the validation gate; it has not gone away, and the whole product-surface justification for alias-first (OPAG-296) is unmet until this lands.

HOW IT GOT PAST LCLI-553's ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, recorded because the mechanism matters more than the bug. AC#2 read: 'profileTypeDeclaresField returns the canonical type's fields when given an alias, SO LORE LINK ACCEPTS AN ALIASED DOCUMENT.' The predicate does return true and a unit test proves it. I checked the criterion against that unit test and never ran the command the criterion's own second clause names. That is substituting a weaker measurement for the one the criterion asked for -- and it is worse than leaving the box unchecked, because a checked box stops anyone else looking. I had ALSO run the end-to-end form earlier in the campaign, before the alias existed, which is precisely what made the unit test feel like a sufficient re-run.

FIX: make the generated type schema accept the canonical name OR any alias (z.literal -> a union/enum over [name, ...aliases]). One consequence to carry deliberately: buildJsonSchema derives the editor JSON Schema from the Zod object, so the emitted schemas gain enum: ["Arc", "Story"] and an editor stops flagging an un-migrated document too. That is wanted, and it means arc.schema.json and story.schema.json stay byte-identical.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A document carrying an ALIAS spelling in its type field passes lore validate and lore check under a profile that declares the canonical type
lore link ACCEPTS that document end-to-end - measured by running the command, not by asserting the predicate it calls
A document carrying an UNDECLARED type is still rejected exactly as before - the fix widens acceptance to declared aliases only
The emitted JSON Schema for both the canonical and alias filenames accepts either spelling, and the two files stay byte-identical
Mutation-tested, and the end-to-end lore link case is one of the predicted reds

implementationNotes:
FIXED AND MEASURED END-TO-END, which is the part LCLI-553 skipped.

Change: buildTypeSchema takes the type's aliases and pins `type` as `z.literal([name, ...aliases])` when there are any, keeping a plain `z.literal(name)` when there are none so an aliasless profile's emitted JSON Schema keeps its existing `const` form byte-for-byte (there is a test asserting exactly that, so the no-churn claim is checkable rather than asserted).

PROOF, run against the local build in a scratch bundle with an Arc+Story-alias profile, three measurements with a positive control rather than one:
  1. REGRESSION TARGET. `lore link stories/legacy TASK-1` on a `type: Story` document now returns "Quest workspace is not initialized" -- it reached the TRACKER, meaning it passed both the coupling gate and the validation gate. Before this fix the same call returned `invalid Story frontmatter ... type: Invalid input: expected "Arc"`.
  2. POSITIVE CONTROL. An UNDECLARED type is still refused: `lore link x/saga TASK-1` -> `cannot link tasks to x/saga: type "Saga" does not declare a tasks field`. So acceptance widened to declared aliases only, not to anything.
  3. EMITTED SCHEMA. `.properties.type` is now `{"type":"string","enum":["Arc","Story"]}`, and arc.schema.json / story.schema.json are byte-identical (cmp). An editor following either modeline stops flagging an un-migrated document, which is wanted and follows from the same change.

TEST-SUITE DEFECT FOUND WHILE DOING THIS, third of the campaign and worth recording. Adding the acceptance tests turned the drift-ownership case RED, correctly: its fixture built `committed` from an ALIASLESS export, whose arc bytes now legitimately differ from the aliased regeneration, so it was genuinely stale. Rebuilt so `committed` is the aliased emission with the alias path ADDED BY THE TEST rather than taken from the emitter's alias output -- which keeps the two sides from moving together while modelling what a migrated repo actually holds. Re-verified: the emitter-drops-aliases mutant still reddens 3 cases, so non-circularity survived the rewrite.

VALIDATION: typecheck clean; bun test 3329 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail across 105 files; biome 3 warnings 0 errors, matching clean origin/dev.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS: LCLI-554's premise. The alias now actually preserves the behaviour the product-surface ruling (OPAG-296) requires, which it did not between #193 and this.
finalSummary: buildTypeSchema now admits alias spellings in the type field (z.literal([name, ...aliases]), plain literal when aliasless so no schema churn). Verified end-to-end against the local build with a positive control: lore link on a type: Story document reaches the tracker, an undeclared type is still refused, and the emitted schema carries enum [Arc, Story] with the alias file byte-identical. Fixes the regression LCLI-553 claimed but did not deliver. Delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#195.
